text: If $𝜖_{0}$ denotes the permittivity of free space and $\Phi _{E}$ is the flux of the electric field through the area bounded by the closed surface, then dimensions of $\left (𝜖_{0}\frac{d𝜙_{E}}{dt}\right )$ are that of :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We can use Gauss’s law to analyze the dimensions. Gauss’s law states that

$\Phi _{E}=\frac{q}{𝜖_{0}},$

where

$\Phi _{E}$ is the electric flux,

$q$ is the electric charge,

$𝜖_{0}$ is the permittivity of free space.

To find the dimensions of $𝜖_{0}\frac{d\Phi _{E}}{dt}$, follow these steps:

Differentiate Gauss’s law with respect to time:

$\frac{d\Phi _{E}}{dt}=\frac{1}{𝜖_{0}}\frac{dq}{dt}.$

Multiply the equation by $𝜖_{0}$:

$𝜖_{0}\frac{d\Phi _{E}}{dt}=\frac{dq}{dt}.$

Recognize that the time rate of change of charge, $\frac{dq}{dt}$, is by definition the electric current.

Thus, the dimensions of $𝜖_{0}\frac{d\Phi _{E}}{dt}$ are those of electric current.

The correct answer is: Option C, electric current.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: The percentage increase in magnetic field (B) when space within a current carrying solenoid is filled with magnesium (magnetic susceptibility $χ_{\mathrm{Mg}}=1.2\times 10^{-5}$ ) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The percentage change in the magnetic field (B) when the space within a current-carrying solenoid is filled with magnesium is calculated as follows:

We start by using the formula for percentage change in the magnetic field:

$%\text{change in}B=\frac{B_{\text{new}}-B_{\text{old}}}{B_{\text{old}}}\times 100%$

Substituting the expressions for the magnetic field, we have:

$=\frac{μni-μ_{0}ni}{μ_{0}ni}\times 100%=\frac{μ-μ_{0}}{μ_{0}}\times 100%$

Where:

$μ$ is the permeability of the material inserted (here, magnesium).

$μ_{0}$ is the permeability of free space.

$n$ is the number of turns per unit length of the solenoid.

$i$ is the current through the solenoid.

Given that the relationship between the permeability of the medium ($μ$) and relative permeability ($μ_{r}$) is:

$μ=μ_{0}μ_{r}$

We can simplify this to:

$=\frac{μ_{0}μ_{r}-μ_{0}}{μ_{0}}\times 100%$

Which reduces to:

$=(μ_{r}-1)\times 100%$

The relative permeability $μ_{r}$ is equal to $1+χ$, where $χ$ is the magnetic susceptibility. Thus, we have:

$=χ\times 100%$

When magnesium is used, with a magnetic susceptibility $χ_{\text{Mg}}=1.2\times 10^{-5}$, the calculation becomes:

$=1.2\times 10^{-5}\times 100%=1.2\times 10^{-3}%$

Therefore, the percentage increase in the magnetic field when the solenoid is filled with magnesium is $1.2\times 10^{-3}%$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force $⃗{F}=\left (2t\hat{i}+3t^{2}\hat{j}\right )N$. The power generated by the force at time $t$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given Information:

Force: $⃗{F}=(2t\hat{i}+3t^{2}\hat{j})\text{N}$

Mass of the object, $m=1000\text{g}=1\text{kg}$

Determine Acceleration:

Using Newton's second law, $\vec{F}=m\vec{a}$.

Thus, the acceleration, $\vec{a}=2t\hat{i}+3t^{2}\hat{j}$.

Velocity Calculation:

To find velocity, integrate acceleration with respect to time:

$\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt}=2t\hat{i}+3t^{2}\hat{j}$

Integrate to find $\vec{v}$:

$\vec{v}=\int (2t\hat{i}+3t^{2}\hat{j})dt=t^{2}\hat{i}+t^{3}\hat{j}+⃗{C}$

(Assuming initial velocity is zero, $⃗{C}=0$, hence $\vec{v}=t^{2}\hat{i}+t^{3}\hat{j}$).

Calculate Power:

Power is defined as the dot product of force and velocity vectors:

$P=\vec{F}\cdot \vec{v}=(2t\hat{i}+3t^{2}\hat{j})\cdot (t^{2}\hat{i}+t^{3}\hat{j})$

Computing the dot product gives:

$P=(2t\cdot t^{2})+(3t^{2}\cdot t^{3})=2t^{3}+3t^{5}$

The power generated at time $t$ is $P=(2t^{3}+3t^{5})\text{W}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
An ac current is represented as

$i=5\sqrt{2}+10\cos \left (650πt+\frac{π}{6}\right )Amp$

The r.m.s value of the current is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the root mean square (RMS) value of the given alternating current, follow these steps:

The current is represented as:

$i=5\sqrt{2}+10\cos \left (650πt+\frac{π}{6}\right )\text{Amp}$

Here, the time-independent DC component is $5\sqrt{2}$ and the AC component is $10\cos \left (650πt+\frac{π}{6}\right )$.

Calculate the square of the current, $i^{2}$:

$i^{2}=\left (5\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}+\left (10\cos \left (650πt+\frac{π}{6}\right )\right )^{2}+2\times 5\sqrt{2}\times 10\cos \left (650πt+\frac{π}{6}\right )$

Simplifying, we have:

$i^{2}=50+100\cos ^{2}\left (650πt+\frac{π}{6}\right )+100\sqrt{2}\cos \left (650πt+\frac{π}{6}\right )$

Find the average value $\langle i^{2}\rangle$:

The average value of $\cos$ terms over a period is zero, simplifying our equation to:

$\langle i^{2}\rangle =50+\frac{100}{2}+0$

This simplifies to:

$\langle i^{2}\rangle =50+50=100$

Calculate the RMS current:

The RMS value is the square root of the mean of the squares of the current:

$i_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{100}=10\text{Amp}$

Thus, the RMS value of the current is 10 Amps.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave $x=\mathrm{a}\cos (1.5\mathrm{t})\cos (50.5\mathrm{t})$ where t is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat. (close to nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The superposition of the two harmonic waves results in the wave equation:

$x=a\cos (1.5t)\cos (50.5t)$

This equation can be expanded using the trigonometric identity for the product of cosines:

$x=\frac{a}{2}\cos [(1.5+50.5)t]+\frac{a}{2}\cos [(50.5-1.5)t]$

Simplifying, we find:

$x=\frac{a}{2}\cos (52t)+\frac{a}{2}\cos (49t)$

This represents two waves with angular frequencies $52$ and $49$, respectively.

To find the beat frequency, we calculate the differences in frequencies:

$f_{1}=\frac{52}{2π},f_{2}=\frac{49}{2π}$

The beat frequency is then:

$f_{\text{Beat}}=f_{1}-f_{2}=\frac{3}{2π}\text{Hz}$

The period of the beats, $T_{\text{Beat}}$, is the reciprocal of the beat frequency:

$T_{\text{Beat}}=\frac{1}{f_{\text{Beat}}}=\frac{2π}{3}\text{\sec }$

Approximating this gives:

$T_{\text{Beat}}\approx 2.09\text{\sec }\approx 2\text{\sec }$

text: Two wires A and B are made of same material having ratio of lengths $\frac{L_{A}}{L_{B}}=\frac{1}{3}$ and their diameters ratio $\frac{d_{A}}{d_{B}}=2$. If both the wires are stretched using same force, what would be the ratio of their respective elongations?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given:

The ratio of lengths: $\frac{L_{A}}{L_{B}}=\frac{1}{3}$

The ratio of diameters: $\frac{d_{A}}{d_{B}}=2$

Both wires are subject to the same stretching force, and since they are made of the same material, their Young's modulus ($Y$) is the same.

The elongation ($\Delta L$) of a wire subject to a force is given by:

$\Delta L=\frac{F\cdot L}{A\cdot Y}$

where $F$ is the force applied, $L$ is the original length, $A$ is the cross-sectional area, and $Y$ is Young's modulus.

For wires $A$ and $B$:

$\Delta L_{A}=\frac{F_{A}\cdot L_{A}}{A_{A}\cdot Y_{A}}$

$\Delta L_{B}=\frac{F_{B}\cdot L_{B}}{A_{B}\cdot Y_{B}}$

Since $F_{A}=F_{B}$ and $Y_{A}=Y_{B}$, the ratio of their elongations becomes:

$\frac{\Delta L_{A}}{\Delta L_{B}}=\frac{L_{A}\cdot A_{B}}{L_{B}\cdot A_{A}}$

The cross-sectional area $A$ is a function of diameter, $A=\frac{π}{4}d^{2}$. Therefore,

$A_{A}=\frac{π}{4}d_{A}^{2}\text{and}A_{B}=\frac{π}{4}d_{B}^{2}$

Substituting these into the elongation ratio:

$\frac{\Delta L_{A}}{\Delta L_{B}}=\left (\frac{L_{A}}{L_{B}}\right )\left (\frac{\frac{π}{4}d_{B}^{2}}{\frac{π}{4}d_{A}^{2}}\right )=\left (\frac{L_{A}}{L_{B}}\right )\left (\frac{d_{B}}{d_{A}}\right )^{2}$

Substitute the given ratios:

$\frac{\Delta L_{A}}{\Delta L_{B}}=\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}=\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )=\frac{1}{12}$

Thus, the ratio of the elongations of wires $A$ and $B$ is $\frac{1}{12}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
Two plane polarized light waves combine at a certain point whose electric field components are

$\begin{array}{l} E_{1}=E_{0}\mathrm{Sin}ωt \\ E_{2}=E_{0}\mathrm{Sin}\left (ωt+\dfrac{π}{3}\right ) \end{array}$

Find the amplitude of the resultant wave.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the amplitude of the resultant wave for the given electric field components, we use the formula for the resultant amplitude of two combining waves. These components are:

$E_{1}=E_{0}\sin ωt$

$E_{2}=E_{0}\sin \left (ωt+\frac{π}{3}\right )$

The general formula for the amplitude $E$ of two superimposed waves $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ with a phase difference is:

$E=\sqrt{E_{1}^{2}+E_{2}^{2}+2E_{1}E_{2}\cos 𝜙}$

where $𝜙$ is the phase difference between the two waves. In this scenario, $𝜙=\frac{π}{3}$.

Substituting the given expressions and phase difference into the formula, we get:

$E=\sqrt{(E_{0})^{2}+(E_{0})^{2}+2(E_{0})(E_{0})\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}\right )}$

Given that $\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=\frac{1}{2}$, this simplifies to:

$E=\sqrt{2E_{0}^{2}+E_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{3}E_{0}$

Thus, the amplitude of the resultant wave is $\sqrt{3}E_{0}\approx 1.73E_{0}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles $(45^{\circ }+α)$ and $(45^{\circ }-α)$ with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the ratio of the times of flight for two projectiles fired from the ground with the same initial speed but at different angles, we follow these steps:

Projectile Angles:

The first projectile is launched at an angle $θ_{1}=45^{\circ }+α$.

The second projectile is launched at an angle $θ_{2}=45^{\circ }-α$.

Time of Flight Formula:

The time of flight $T$ for a projectile is given by:

$T=\frac{2v\sin θ}{g}$

where $v$ is the initial speed and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

Ratio of Times of Flight:

The ratio of the times of flights $\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}$ can be determined as follows:

$\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{\sin (45^{\circ }+α)}{\sin (45^{\circ }-α)}$

Applying Trigonometric Identities:

Use the sine addition and subtraction formulas:

$\sin (45^{\circ }+α)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\cos α+\sin α)$

$\sin (45^{\circ }-α)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\cos α-\sin α)$

Simplifying the Ratio:

Substitute the expressions for $\sin (45^{\circ }+α)$ and $\sin (45^{\circ }-α)$ into the ratio:

$\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\cos α+\sin α)}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\cos α-\sin α)}=\frac{\cos α+\sin α}{\cos α-\sin α}$

Factor out the trigonometric functions to express in terms of tangent:

$\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{1+\tan α}{1-\tan α}$

Therefore, the ratio of the times of flights for the two projectiles is $\frac{1+\tan α}{1-\tan α}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: In a hydrogen like ion, the energy difference between the $2^{\text{nd}}$ excitation energy state and ground is 108.8 eV . The atomic number of the ion is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the atomic number (Z) of a hydrogen-like ion, given that the energy difference between its second excitation state and the ground state is 108.8 eV, we use the following formula for the energy difference between two energy levels in a hydrogen-like atom:

$\Delta E=13.6\text{eV}\times Z^{2}\left [\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right ]$

Here, for the second excitation, $n_{2}=3$ (since excitation means moving to the second higher energy level beyond the ground state, which means $n_{1}=1$ for the ground state to $n_{2}=3$). Plug these into the energy difference formula:

$\Delta E=13.6Z^{2}\left [\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{3^{2}}\right ]$

Simplifying the term in brackets:

$\Delta E=13.6Z^{2}\left [1-\frac{1}{9}\right ]=13.6Z^{2}\times \frac{8}{9}$

Given that $\Delta E=108.8\text{eV}$, set the equations equal:

$13.6\frac{8Z^{2}}{9}=108.8$

Solving for $Z$, first simplify:

$13.6\times \frac{8}{9}\times Z^{2}=108.8$

$\frac{108.8\times 9}{13.6\times 8}=Z^{2}$

$Z^{2}=9$

Thus, the atomic number $Z$ is:

$Z=3$ 

The atomic number of the ion is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: Two thin convex lenses of focal lengths 30 cm and 10 cm are placed coaxially, 10 cm apart. The power of this combination is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the power of a combination of two thin convex lenses, we use the formula for the equivalent focal length $f_{\text{eq}}$ of the lens system when the lenses are placed coaxially with a certain distance $d$ between them:

$\frac{1}{f_{\text{eq}}}=\frac{1}{f_{1}}+\frac{1}{f_{2}}-\frac{d}{f_{1}f_{2}}$

Given:

$f_{1}=30\text{cm}$ 

$f_{2}=10\text{cm}$

$d=10\text{cm}$ (distance between the two lenses)

First, convert the focal lengths from centimeters to meters:

$f_{1}=0.3\text{m}$

$f_{2}=0.1\text{m}$

Plug in the values into the equation:

$\frac{1}{f_{\text{eq}}}=\frac{1}{0.3}+\frac{1}{0.1}-\frac{0.1}{(0.3)(0.1)}$

Calculate each term:

$\frac{1}{0.3}=\frac{10}{3}\approx 3.33$

$\frac{1}{0.1}=10$

$\frac{0.1}{(0.3)(0.1)}=\frac{0.1}{0.03}=\frac{10}{3}\approx 3.33$

Substitute these calculated values back into the formula:

$\frac{1}{f_{\text{eq}}}=3.33+10-3.33$

$\frac{1}{f_{\text{eq}}}=10$

Thus, the power of the lens combination is:

$\text{Power}=\frac{1}{f_{\text{eq}}}=10\text{D}$

Therefore, the power of the lens system is 10 diopters (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
Two charges $q_{1}$ and $q_{2}$ are separated by a distance of 30 cm . A third charge $q_{3}$ initially at ' C ' as shown in the figure, is moved along the circular path of radius 40 cm from C to D . If the difference in potential energy due to movement of $q_{3}$ from C to D is given by $\frac{q_{3}\mathrm{K}}{4π𝜖_{0}}$, the value of K is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the figure, $q_{1}$ is at A, the centre of the circular path of radius $40\text{cm}$, and $q_{2}$ is at B on AD with $AB=30\text{cm}$.

The distance of $q_{3}$ from $q_{1}$ stays $0.4\text{m}$, so the interaction energy of $q_{3}$ with $q_{1}$ does not change.

Distance of $q_{2}$ from C: $BC=\sqrt{AB^{2}+AC^{2}}=\sqrt{0.3^{2}+0.4^{2}}=0.5\text{m}$.

Distance of $q_{2}$ from D: $BD=AD-AB=0.4-0.3=0.1\text{m}$.

$\Delta U=\dfrac{q_{2}q_{3}}{4π𝜖_{0}}\left (\dfrac{1}{0.1}-\dfrac{1}{0.5}\right )=\dfrac{q_{2}q_{3}}{4π𝜖_{0}}(10-2)=\dfrac{q_{3}(8q_{2})}{4π𝜖_{0}}$

Comparing with $\dfrac{q_{3}K}{4π𝜖_{0}}$ gives $K=8q_{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
A lens having refractive index 1.6 has focal length of 12 cm , when it is in air. Find the focal length of the lens when it is placed in water.
(Take refractive index of water as 1.28)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the focal length of a lens with a refractive index of 1.6 when placed in water, given that its focal length in air is 12 cm and the refractive index of water is 1.28, we can use the lens maker's formula:

$\frac{1}{f}=\left (\frac{μ_{L}}{μ_{m}}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

When the lens is in air, the refractive index of the medium, $μ_{m}$, is 1. Therefore, for the lens in air:

$\frac{1}{12}=(1.6-1)\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

Simplifying gives:

$\frac{1}{12}=\frac{6}{10}\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

Solving for $\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$:

$\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}=\frac{10}{72}$

Now, when the lens is placed in water, $μ_{m}=1.28$. Substituting into the equation gives:

$\frac{1}{f}=\left (\frac{1.6}{1.28}-1\right )\left (\frac{10}{72}\right )$

Calculating each part:

$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{32}{128}\times \frac{10}{72}$

$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{4}\times \frac{10}{72}$

Hence, solving for $f$:

$f=28.8\text{cm}=288\text{mm}$

Thus, the focal length of the lens in water is 288 mm.

text:
Match the List I with List II

  
    
    List - I
    
    List - II
  

  
    (A)
    Triatomic rigid gas
    (I)
    $\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}=\frac{5}{3}$
  
  
    (B)
    Diatomic non-rigid gas
    (II)
    $\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}=\frac{7}{5}$
  
  
    (C)
    Monoatomic gas
    (III)
    $\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}=\frac{4}{3}$
  
  
    (D)
    Diatomic rigid gas
    (IV)
    $\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}=\frac{9}{7}$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The explanation uses the equation for the heat capacity ratio, $γ=1+\frac{2}{\text{f}}$, where $\text{f}$ is the degrees of freedom of the gas. Here's how it applies to different types of gases:

Triatomic Rigid Gas:  

Degrees of freedom ($\text{f}$) = 6

$γ=1+\frac{2}{6}=\frac{4}{3}$

Diatomic Non-Rigid Gas:  

Degrees of freedom ($\text{f}$) = 7

$γ=1+\frac{2}{7}=\frac{9}{7}$

Diatomic Rigid Gas:  

Degrees of freedom ($\text{f}$) = 5

$γ=1+\frac{2}{5}=\frac{7}{5}$

Monoatomic Gas:  

Degrees of freedom ($\text{f}$) = 3

$γ=1+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{5}{3}$

Therefore, when matching List I with List II, the correct pairing is:

A (Triatomic rigid gas) - III $(\frac{4}{3})$

B (Diatomic non-rigid gas) - IV $(\frac{9}{7})$

C (Monoatomic gas) - I $(\frac{5}{3})$

D (Diatomic rigid gas) - II $(\frac{7}{5})$

Thus, the correct answer from the options given is:

A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

text:
A wire of length 10 cm and diameter 0.5 mm is used in a bulb. The temperature of the wire is $1727^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ and power radiated by the wire is 94.2 W . Its emissivity is $\frac{x}{8}$ where $x=$ $_________$.

(Given $σ=6.0\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{W}\mathrm{m}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-4},π=3.14$ and assume that the emissivity of wire material is same at all wavelength.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $L=0.1\text{m}$, $d=0.5\text{mm}=5\times 10^{-4}\text{m}$ and $T=1727+273=2000\text{K}$.

Radiation leaves the curved surface of the wire (the end faces are negligible), so

$A=2πrL=πdL=3.14\times 5\times 10^{-4}\times 0.1=1.57\times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{2}$

By Stefan's law, a body of emissivity $e$ radiates $P=eσAT^{4}$, where

$σAT^{4}=6.0\times 10^{-8}\times 1.57\times 10^{-4}\times 1.6\times 10^{13}=150.72\text{W}$

$e=\dfrac{94.2}{150.72}=0.625=\dfrac{5}{8}\Rightarrow x=5$

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
For ac circuit shown in figure, $\mathrm{R}=100\mathrm{k}\Omega$ and $\mathrm{C}=100\mathrm{pF}$ and the phase difference between $\mathrm{V}_{\text{in}}$ and $(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}})$ is $90^{\circ }$. The input signal frequency is $10^{x}\mathrm{rad}/\sec$, where ' $x$ ' is $__________$ .


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Both branches are connected across $V_{\text{in}}$, and potentials are measured from the lower common wire. In the left branch ($R$ above, $C$ below) $V_{A}$ is the voltage across $C$; in the right branch ($C$ above, $R$ below) $V_{B}$ is the voltage across $R$.

The two branches have the same $R$ and $C$, so their currents have equal amplitude and each leads $V_{\text{in}}$ by the same angle $𝜙$, where

$\tan 𝜙=\dfrac{X_{C}}{R},X_{C}=\dfrac{1}{ωC}$

In each branch the resistor voltage $V_{\text{in}}\cos 𝜙$ is in phase with the current (angle $𝜙$ ahead of $V_{\text{in}}$), and the capacitor voltage $V_{\text{in}}\sin 𝜙$ lags the current by $90^{\circ }$ (angle $𝜙-90^{\circ }$).

So $V_{B}$ is a phasor of length $V_{\text{in}}\cos 𝜙$ at angle $𝜙$, and $-V_{A}$ is a phasor of length $V_{\text{in}}\sin 𝜙$ at angle $𝜙+90^{\circ }$. Being perpendicular, they add to a phasor of length $V_{\text{in}}$ turned further by $α$, with $\tan α=\dfrac{\sin 𝜙}{\cos 𝜙}$, so $α=𝜙$.

Hence $V_{B}-V_{A}$ leads $V_{\text{in}}$ by $2𝜙$. For a phase difference of $90^{\circ }$:

$2𝜙=90^{\circ }\Rightarrow 𝜙=45^{\circ }\Rightarrow X_{C}=R\Rightarrow ω=\dfrac{1}{RC}$

$ω=\dfrac{1}{(100\times 10^{3})(100\times 10^{-12})}=\dfrac{1}{10^{-5}}=10^{5}\text{rad s}^{-1}$

So $x=5$.

Hence, the answer is 5.

text: A container contains a liquid with refractive index of 1.2 up to a height of 60 cm and another liquid having refractive index 1.6 is added to height H above first liquid. If viewed from above, the apparent shift in the position of bottom of container is 40 cm . The value of H is $________ cm . ($Consider liquids are immisible)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} y=\text{apparent depth of bottom} \\ \dfrac{y}{1}=\dfrac{H}{1.6}+\dfrac{60}{1.2} \\ \text{Shift}=40 \\ H+60-y=40 \\ H+60-\dfrac{\mathrm{H}}{1.6}-\dfrac{60}{1.2}=40 \\ \dfrac{6}{16}\mathrm{H}=30 \\ H=80\mathrm{cm} \end{array}$

text:
An ideal gas has undergone through the cyclic process as shown in the figure. Work done by the gas in the entire cycle is $________$ $\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{J}$.
(Take $π=3.14$ )


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The work done by the gas in a cycle equals, in magnitude, the area enclosed by the closed loop on the $P$–$V$ diagram.

The loop is an ellipse centred at $(400\text{kPa},250\text{cm}^{3})$; it spans $300$ to $500\text{kPa}$ along $P$ and $150$ to $350\text{cm}^{3}$ along $V$, so its semi-axes are

$a=\dfrac{500-300}{2}\text{kPa}=100\text{kPa}=1\times 10^{5}\text{Pa},b=\dfrac{350-150}{2}\text{cm}^{3}=100\text{cm}^{3}=1\times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{3}$

The area of an ellipse is $πab$:

$W=πab=3.14\times \left (1\times 10^{5}\right )\times \left (1\times 10^{-4}\right )\text{J}=31.4\text{J}=314\times 10^{-1}\text{J}$

Hence, the answer is 314.
